standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation triangles
standard_prerequisites.use: Distinguished triangles H^{-n-1}(E)[n+1] -> K_{n+1} -> K_n -> H^{-n-1}(E)[n+2].

standard_prerequisites.name: Stalkwise injectivity criterion
standard_prerequisites.use: Injectivity of H^m(R lim K_n)_x -> H^m(K_{n(x)})_x from the two per-point assumptions.

core_obligations: Reduction: it suffices to find n(x) >= -m with H^m(K)_x -> H^m(K_{n(x)})_x injective, since then the composition H^m(E)_x -> H^m(K)_x -> H^m(K_{n(x)})_x is a bijection (proof lines 9640-9655).

Set n(x) = 1 + max{-m, p(x, m-1) - m, -1 + p(x, m) - m, -2 + p(x, m+1) - m}; claim that H^{m-1}(U,K_{n+1}) -> H^{m-1}(U,K_n) and H^m(U,K_{n+1}) -> H^m(U,K_n) are isomorphisms for n >= n(x) and U  in  U_x: from the truncation triangles H^{-n-1}(E)[n+1] -> K_{n+1} -> K_n -> H^{-n-1}(E)[n+2] and the vanishing of the three displayed groups under the assumption of the lemma (proof lines 9656-9687).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to stalkwise injectivity with the derived-limit-injective lemma.
Choose n(x) explicitly and verify the transition isomorphisms from the truncation triangle.
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces to stalkwise injectivity via the derived-limit-injective lemma; the key claim that the transition maps on H^{m-1} and H^m are isomorphisms follows from the long exact sequence of the truncation triangle and the explicit choice of n(x).
